Keep Node.js and Commander. The local prohibition on parser/runtime changes takes precedence over mytech defaults, and the supplied facts give no reason to introduce Effect. Mytech also prefers Commander for a CLI without an independent need for Effect; its extra-typings preference is not evidence that this project lacks or needs that dependency. [Decision posture and precedence](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/README.md), [TypeScript CLI guidance](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/libraries/typescript/cli.md).

The actionable gap is stdout: human logs mixed with result JSON prevent automation from treating it as one structured document. Define or repair the machine-readable invocation so stdout contains at most one complete, newline-terminated JSON document, with logs/progress on stderr and quiet operation supported. Ensure dependency logging follows the same rule. Preserve the existing parser/runtime while making this output contract explicit. [Automation process contract](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/practices/automation-facing-cli-contracts.md).

Specify stable success/failure structure and exit statuses for success, execution failure, and invalid invocation. Their current behavior was not supplied, so these are checks to resolve, not additional confirmed defects. Verify the packaged CLI as an external process on success and failure, parsing the complete stdout stream and checking its trailing newline, stderr policy, and exit status. [CLI verification](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/practices/automation-facing-cli-contracts.md), [Consumer-boundary verification](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/practices/verification-from-source-to-consumer.md).
